# Q-M1f.348 — A generated file says it is generated and names no tool

A file of the project that a program writes says so at its head: that it is generated, and that an edit by hand is
lost the next time it is written. It does not name the program that writes it, which is part of the work on Ein and
not of Ein ([Q-M1f.345](Q-M1f.345-nothing-in-the-project-reads-links-or-names.md)). A section of a page that a
program writes is marked as such where it starts and ends, and says the same.

**Why.** What a reader of the file needs is that it is not the place to edit; where its generator lives is a fact
about the work, which changes with the work.

**Held by.** The heads of the generated files: `stdlib/math/digits.ein`, `stdlib/math/bits.ein` and
`stdlib/math/num9.ein`, the rows of `stdlib/bool/gates.ein`, the generated programs of `examples/arith/`
(`long_numbers.ein`, `many_calculations.ein`, `factorial.ein`), and the two grammar blocks of
`docs/ein/user/reference/grammar.md`, marked `generated` where they start and end.
